title: Add RAG telemetry probes workshop quickstart and local playground
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation and summary: This PR adds a small, opinionated quickstart that teaches engineers how to instrument RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agents with telemetry probes and visualizations backed by the Redwood Console. The goal is hands-on learning: developers should be able to run a local sandbox, exercise an agent end-to-end, and observe token-level latency, KV cache hit/miss signals, batching behavior, and per-tool invocation traces in the Console.

What this PR includes: a) telemetry-workshop/ - a compact quickstart with Docker Compose and a one-file node agent shim that performs simple retrieval + tool-calling; b) telemetry-workshop/playground/ - a lightweight browser UI that submits example scenarios and displays trace IDs returned by the runtime; c) sample prompts and eval harness used for the workshop; d) README with step-by-step instructions for local run, Console integration, and validating telemetry signals; e) CI smoke test that runs the Docker Compose sandbox and asserts the agent returns expected JSON schema and that the runtime exposes a /metrics endpoint.

Design notes and constraints: The quickstart intentionally uses a tiny open model (quantized) and in-memory retrieval index to keep the surface area small. Telemetry events are emitted via the platform-compatible tracing shim so traces appear in a customer's Console when run against a Private or Dedicated deployment; locally the quickstart ships an optional adapter that collects traces to an export file for offline inspection. The README explains how to swap the adapter to forward traces to a Redwood Console endpoint (using a user API key).

Developer checklist (included in README as a checklist): - Checkout repo and cd into telemetry-workshop - Copy .env.example to .env and optionally set REDWOOD_API_KEY to forward traces - Start docker-compose up --build - Wait for the agent to register and visit the local playground at http://localhost:8080 - Run the smoke script ./scripts/smoke.sh to validate /metrics and a sample chat flow - Inspect traces: either open trace_export/*.json or (if forwarding) open Redwood Console -> Traces -> filter by demo-workshop

Testing and CI: The PR adds a GH Action workflow under .github/workflows/telemetry-workshop-smoke.yml that spins up the compose sandbox, hits the playground API, checks the agent returns a structured tool call and final answer, and hits the runtime /metrics endpoint to assert presence of batching and kv_cache_{hit,miss} counters. The CI run passed after fixing a flaky port binding in docker-compose (see commit history).

Backward compatibility and security: This quickstart is docs-only and opt-in; it does not change runtime code paths. Sensitive config like API keys are read from env and never committed. The README includes guidance for customers running the quickstart in air-gapped or VPC environments.

Usage guidance for customers: The README contains a short section showing how operators can map workshop telemetry signals to Redwood Console dashboards: token latency heatmap, per-route batching distribution, and tool-invocation waterfall charts. There is also a short troubleshooting section for common local issues (port collisions, missing model files, Docker resources).

Related work: references to ENG-1284 (telemetry v2 rollout), the RAG authoring quickstarts, and a doc PR that will add a Console dashboard template (separate PR).

Notes for reviewers: I focused on minimal, copyable examples (no runtime modifications). Please check the README for clarity, ensure the smoke CI assertions are robust but not brittle, and verify the trace export format is easy to import into the Console or to visualize locally.

Merge: squashed and merged after approvals.
